guide.what: A noun (sustantivo) names a person, place, thing or idea. In Spanish every noun is masculine or feminine, and the words around it (el/la, adjectives) change to match.

rules.t: Learn every noun with its article
rules.d: Gender is part of the word. Learn «la casa», not just «casa». Most nouns ending in -o are masculine and most ending in -a are feminine, but not all.
rules.ex: el libro, la mesa, el problema, la mano
rules.exEn: the book, the table, the problem, the hand

rules.t: Endings that tell you the gender
rules.d: Feminine: -ción, -sión, -dad, -tad, -tud, -umbre. Masculine: -aje, -or, -ma (from Greek: problema, sistema, tema, programa).
rules.ex: la canción, la ciudad, el viaje, el idioma
rules.exEn: the song, the city, the trip, the language

rules.d: Ending in a vowel: add -s. Ending in a consonant: add -es. -z changes to -ces. Words ending in unstressed -s stay the same.
rules.ex: casa → casas · ciudad → ciudades · vez → veces · la crisis → las crisis
rules.exEn: house → houses · city → cities · time → times · the crisis → the crises

rules.t: Accents can appear or disappear in the plural
rules.d: To keep the stress in the same place, some plurals lose or gain a written accent.
rules.ex: la canción → las canciones · el joven → los jóvenes
rules.exEn: the song → the songs · the young man → young people

rules.t: El before a stressed a- with feminine nouns
rules.d: Feminine nouns that start with a stressed a- or ha- take el and un in the singular, to avoid two a-sounds together. They are still feminine: adjectives and the plural use the feminine.
rules.ex: el agua fría · las aguas · el hambre
rules.exEn: the cold water · the waters · hunger

rules.d: Many words for people have a feminine form (el hijo / la hija, el profesor / la profesora). Words ending in -ista or -nte usually keep one form and change only the article.
rules.ex: el estudiante / la estudiante · el periodista / la periodista

rules.t: Same word, different gender, different meaning
rules.d: A few nouns change meaning with the article.
rules.ex: el capital (money) / la capital (city) · el orden (order, tidiness) / la orden (a command)

rules.t: Spanish uses the article more than English
rules.d: Use the article for things in general and for abstract ideas, where English uses no article.
rules.ex: Me gusta el café. La salud es importante.
rules.exEn: I like coffee. Health is important.

mistakes.why: Words from Greek ending in -ma are masculine: el problema, el tema, el sistema.
Mano is feminine even though it ends in -o. Also la foto, la moto, la radio.
Stressed a- at the start takes el, but the adjective stays feminine (fría).

mistakes.wrong: Soy un estudiante de Panamá y me gustan perros.
mistakes.right: Soy estudiante de Panamá y me gustan los perros.
mistakes.why: No un/una with a profession after ser; use los for things in general.
Nouns ending in -z change to -ces in the plural: lápiz → lápices.
Información, gente and consejo (advice) work differently from English: información is usually singular; la gente takes a singular verb.

items.use: Use vez for 'how many times', never tiempo. Key phrases: a veces (sometimes), otra vez (again), una vez (once), de vez en cuando (now and then), tal vez (maybe).
items.ex: He ido a Boquete tres veces.
items.exEn: I've been to Boquete three times.

items.use: Ends in -a but is masculine: el día, buenos días. Common: todos los días (every day), hoy en día (nowadays), al día siguiente (the next day).
items.ex: Trabajo todos los días menos el domingo.
items.exEn: I work every day except Sunday.

items.use: Age uses tener: tengo 30 años (not soy 30). Always write the ñ: ano is a very different word.
items.ex: Mi hija tiene cinco años.
items.exEn: My daughter is five years old.

items.use: Los padres can mean 'parents' (mother and father), not only 'fathers'. Madre is a separate word for mother.
items.ex: Mis padres viven en Chitré.
items.exEn: My parents live in Chitré.
items.latam: In Mexico and some countries '¡qué padre!' means 'how cool!'. Not used that way in Panama.

items.use: Thank for something with por: gracias por la ayuda. Gracias a means 'thanks to' (because of): gracias a ti.
items.ex: Muchas gracias por tu ayuda.
items.exEn: Thank you very much for your help.

items.use: Very general word for objects and ideas. Otra cosa = something else; cualquier cosa = anything; la cosa es que... = the thing is...
items.ex: Tengo muchas cosas que hacer hoy.
items.exEn: I have a lot of things to do today.
items.latam: In Panama people often say 'vaina' informally for 'thing': ¿Qué es esa vaina?

items.use: Use el when talking about someone (el señor Pérez), but drop it when talking to them (Buenos días, señor Pérez). Señora is a married or older woman, Mrs.
items.ex: El señor de la tienda es muy amable.
items.exEn: The man at the store is very kind.

items.use: Female counterpart is mujer. ¡Hombre! is also an exclamation of surprise or agreement, like 'Come on!' or 'Of course!'.
items.ex: Ese hombre es mi vecino.
items.exEn: That man is my neighbor.

items.use: Tiempo is time as an amount, not an occurrence (that is vez) or clock time (that is hora). Also weather: ¿Qué tiempo hace? Phrases: a tiempo (on time), hace tiempo (a long time ago).
items.ex: No tengo tiempo para almorzar.
items.exEn: I don't have time to have lunch.

items.use: No article for 'home' after en, a, de: estoy en casa, voy a casa. With an article it means a specific house: la casa de Ana.
items.ex: Hoy me quedo en casa.
items.exEn: Today I'm staying home.

items.use: Decir la verdad = tell the truth. ¿Verdad? at the end of a sentence means 'right?'. De verdad = really, seriously.
items.ex: Es bonito, ¿verdad?
items.exEn: It's pretty, right?

items.use: Ganarse la vida = earn a living. Toda la vida = all my life / forever. Mi vida is a term of affection (darling).
items.ex: La vida en la ciudad es cara.
items.exEn: Life in the city is expensive.

items.use: Used for children, teens and young adults. Chicos can mean 'guys' for a mixed group: ¡Hola, chicos!
items.ex: Los chicos están jugando en el parque.
items.exEn: The kids are playing in the park.
items.latam: In Panama, kids and young people are very often called 'pelaos' (pelao / pelaíta) informally.

items.use: Buenas noches is both 'good evening' and 'good night'. Esta noche = tonight; anoche = last night; de noche / en la noche = at night.
items.ex: Esta noche vamos a cenar afuera.
items.exEn: Tonight we're going out for dinner.
items.latam: Latin America says 'en la noche'; Spain prefers 'por la noche'.

items.use: Hijos means 'children' (sons and daughters): ¿Tienes hijos? = Do you have children? Mijo / mija (mi hijo) is an affectionate address.
items.ex: Tenemos dos hijos: un niño y una niña.
items.exEn: We have two children: a boy and a girl.

items.use: Por favor = please. Hacer un favor = do a favor; pedir un favor = ask a favor. A favor de = in favor of.
items.ex: ¿Me puedes hacer un favor?
items.exEn: Can you do me a favor?

items.use: Hacerse amigos = become friends. Un amigo mío = a friend of mine. Amigos can be a mixed group of male and female friends.
items.ex: Voy al cine con unos amigos.
items.exEn: I'm going to the movies with some friends.
items.latam: In Panama, close friends call each other 'fren' (from English 'friend') or 'compa'.

items.use: Very common in de hecho = in fact, actually. El hecho de que usually takes the subjunctive: el hecho de que no venga...
items.ex: De hecho, ya terminé el informe.
items.exEn: In fact, I already finished the report.

items.use: Keep the accent: papa means potato (la papa) or the Pope (el papa). Mis papás = my parents (informal).
items.ex: Mi papá trabaja en el Canal.
items.exEn: My dad works at the Canal.
items.latam: In Latin America 'mis papás' for 'my parents' is very common; Spain says 'mis padres'.

items.use: Buscar trabajo = look for a job; ir al trabajo = go to work. Also a school or university paper: un trabajo sobre historia.
items.ex: Salgo del trabajo a las cinco.
items.exEn: I get off work at five.

items.use: Mi mujer can mean 'my wife', but esposa is more neutral and polite in Latin America.
items.ex: Esa mujer es la nueva directora.
items.exEn: That woman is the new director.

items.use: Common: en todas partes (everywhere), por otra parte (on the other hand), de parte de (on behalf of), la mayor parte (most). On the phone: ¿De parte de quién? = Who's calling?
items.ex: La mayor parte del día estoy en la oficina.
items.exEn: I'm at the office most of the day.

items.use: Estar de acuerdo (con) = to agree (never 'soy de acuerdo'). De acuerdo alone = OK. Llegar a un acuerdo = reach an agreement.
items.ex: Estoy de acuerdo contigo.
items.exEn: I agree with you.

items.use: Un momento = just a moment. En este momento = right now. De momento / por el momento = for now.
items.ex: Un momento, por favor.
items.exEn: One moment, please.

items.use: Todo el mundo means 'everybody', and takes a singular verb: todo el mundo sabe (everyone knows).
items.ex: Todo el mundo habla de la noticia.
items.exEn: Everybody is talking about the news.

items.use: Gente is singular in Spanish: la gente es amable (not 'son'). The plural gentes is rare. For a counted number use personas: diez personas.
items.ex: La gente aquí es muy amable.
items.exEn: People here are very friendly.

items.use: Niños means 'children' for a mixed group. De niño = as a child: de niño vivía en Colón.
items.ex: Los niños van a la escuela a las siete.
items.exEn: The children go to school at seven.
items.latam: Informal Panamanian Spanish says 'pelao' / 'pelaíta' for a kid.

items.use: Ask the time with ¿Qué hora es? (not ¿Qué tiempo es?). Ya es hora de... = it's about time to... A la hora = on time.
items.ex: ¿A qué hora empieza la reunión?
items.exEn: What time does the meeting start?

items.use: Masculine even though it ends in -a: el problema, un problema serio. No hay problema = no problem.
items.ex: Tenemos un problema con el aire acondicionado.
items.exEn: We have a problem with the air conditioning.

items.use: Tener lugar = take place (happen). En lugar de = instead of. En primer lugar = first of all.
items.ex: La boda tendrá lugar en Casco Viejo.
items.exEn: The wedding will take place in Casco Viejo.

items.use: Always feminine, even for a man: Juan es una persona muy seria. Use personas for counting people: cinco personas.
items.ex: Mi jefe es una persona muy justa.
items.exEn: My boss is a very fair person.

items.use: ¿Qué tipo de...? = What kind of...? Informally, un tipo = a guy. Tipo de cambio = exchange rate.
items.ex: ¿Qué tipo de música te gusta?
items.exEn: What kind of music do you like?

items.use: Uncountable, so singular: el dinero está en el banco. Ahorrar dinero = save money; gastar dinero = spend money.
items.ex: No tengo suficiente dinero para el viaje.
items.exEn: I don't have enough money for the trip.
items.latam: Across Latin America 'plata' is the everyday word for money. In Panama 'billete' is also common: no tengo billete.

items.use: La mañana = the morning; mañana (no article) = tomorrow. Mañana en la mañana = tomorrow morning. Pasado mañana = the day after tomorrow.
items.ex: Corro todas las mañanas en la Cinta Costera.
items.exEn: I run every morning on the Cinta Costera.
items.latam: Latin America says 'en la mañana'; Spain says 'por la mañana'.

items.use: Hermanos can mean brothers and sisters together: ¿Cuántos hermanos tienes? Medio hermano = half brother.
items.ex: Tengo dos hermanos y una hermana.
items.exEn: I have two brothers and a sister.

items.use: Ends in -o but is feminine: la mano, las manos limpias. Dar la mano = shake hands. A mano = by hand; de segunda mano = second-hand.
items.ex: Lávate las manos antes de comer.
items.exEn: Wash your hands before eating.

items.use: En caso de = in case of; en ese caso = in that case. Hacer caso = pay attention, listen to: no me hace caso.
items.ex: Mi hijo nunca me hace caso.
items.exEn: My son never listens to me.

items.use: Ends in -e and is masculine: el nombre. Ask with ¿Cuál es tu nombre? or ¿Cómo te llamas? A nombre de = in the name of.
items.ex: La reserva está a nombre de García.
items.exEn: The reservation is under the name García.

items.use: De esta forma = this way; de todas formas = anyway. Estar en forma = be in shape (fit). False friend: a form to fill in is a formulario.
items.ex: De todas formas, gracias por venir.
items.exEn: Anyway, thanks for coming.

items.use: Darse cuenta (de) = realize. La cuenta, por favor = the check, please. Tener en cuenta = keep in mind. Cuenta bancaria = bank account.
items.ex: No me di cuenta de la hora.
items.exEn: I didn't realize what time it was.

items.use: Tener razón = be right (never 'ser correcto' for people). No tener razón = be wrong. ¿Por qué razón? = for what reason?
items.ex: Tienes razón, es muy tarde.
items.exEn: You're right, it's very late.

items.use: No tengo ni idea = I have no idea. ¡Buena idea! = good idea. Cambiar de idea = change your mind.
items.ex: No tengo ni idea de dónde está.
items.exEn: I have no idea where it is.

items.use: El pasado = the past (noun). As an adjective it means 'last': la semana pasada (last week), el año pasado (last year).
items.ex: No quiero hablar del pasado.
items.exEn: I don't want to talk about the past.

items.use: Fin de semana = weekend. La semana pasada / que viene = last / next week. Entre semana = on weekdays. Semana Santa = Holy Week.
items.ex: Este fin de semana vamos a la playa.
items.exEn: This weekend we're going to the beach.

items.use: Singular verb: mi familia es grande. False friend: familiar as a noun means 'relative' (un familiar = a relative).
items.ex: Toda mi familia vive en David.
items.exEn: My whole family lives in David.

items.use: La policía = the police (the force), with a singular verb. El/la policía = a police officer. Llamar a la policía = call the police.
items.ex: Un policía me ayudó a encontrar la calle.
items.exEn: A police officer helped me find the street.

items.use: Country as a nation. For the countryside (not the city) use el campo. Keep the accent: país, países.
items.ex: Panamá es un país pequeño pero diverso.
items.exEn: Panama is a small but diverse country.

items.use: Dentro de diez minutos = in ten minutes. Un minutito = just a minute (friendly).
items.ex: El bus llega en cinco minutos.
items.exEn: The bus arrives in five minutes.

items.use: Means both 'history' and 'story': la historia de Panamá, una historia de amor. Cuento is a short story or tale, often for children.
items.ex: Me contó una historia muy triste.
items.exEn: He told me a very sad story.

items.use: Masculine: el amor. Hacer el amor = make love. Mi amor is a common term of affection for partners and children.
items.ex: Mi amor, ¿ya comiste?
items.exEn: Honey, did you eat already?

items.use: Al lado de = next to. Por un lado... por otro lado = on one hand... on the other. En todos lados = everywhere.
items.ex: El banco está al lado del supermercado.
items.exEn: The bank is next to the supermarket.

items.use: Same meaning as forma and modo. De esta manera = this way; de ninguna manera = no way. Buenas maneras = good manners.
items.ex: No hay otra manera de hacerlo.
items.exEn: There is no other way to do it.

items.use: Me duele la cabeza = I have a headache (use la, not mi, with body parts). Perder la cabeza = lose your mind.
items.ex: Me duele mucho la cabeza.
items.exEn: I have a bad headache.

items.use: En punto = on the dot (a las tres en punto). Estar a punto de = be about to. Punto de vista = point of view.
items.ex: Estaba a punto de llamarte.
items.exEn: I was about to call you.

items.use: El mes que viene = next month. Al mes = per month (pago 500 al mes). Months are written in lowercase: enero, febrero.
items.ex: Pago el alquiler a principios de mes.
items.exEn: I pay the rent at the beginning of the month.

items.use: Words ending in -dad are feminine: la ciudad. In Panama, 'la ciudad' often means Panama City.
items.ex: Vivo en la ciudad, pero trabajo en Colón.
items.exEn: I live in the city, but I work in Colón.

items.use: Tíos can mean uncle and aunt together: mis tíos. Keep the accent.
items.ex: Mis tíos viven en Santiago.
items.exEn: My aunt and uncle live in Santiago.
items.latam: In Spain 'tío/tía' is slang for 'guy/girl' or 'dude'. In Latin America it normally just means uncle/aunt.

items.use: Abrir / cerrar la puerta = open / close the door. Tocar la puerta = knock on the door. Also an airport gate: puerta 12.
items.ex: Alguien está tocando la puerta.
items.exEn: Someone is knocking on the door.

items.use: Dar tu palabra = give your word. En otras palabras = in other words. ¿Qué significa esta palabra? = What does this word mean?
items.ex: No entiendo esta palabra.
items.exEn: I don't understand this word.

items.use: ¡Ojo! alone is a warning: careful! watch out! Costar un ojo de la cara = cost an arm and a leg.
items.ex: Tiene los ojos verdes.
items.exEn: She has green eyes.

items.use: Feminine, but takes el in the singular because it starts with stressed a-: el agua fría, but las aguas. Adjectives stay feminine.
items.ex: ¿Me trae un vaso de agua, por favor?
items.exEn: Could you bring me a glass of water, please?

items.use: En medio de = in the middle of. Los medios (de comunicación) = the media. Medio ambiente = environment. Por medio de = by means of.
items.ex: Hay un árbol en medio de la calle.
items.exEn: There's a tree in the middle of the street.

items.use: Mostly an adjective (estar loco), but el loco / la loca = the crazy one. Volverse loco = go crazy. Can be offensive about mental illness, so use with care.
items.ex: Manejaba como un loco.
items.exEn: He was driving like a madman.

items.use: Fin de semana = weekend. Por fin = finally (after waiting). Al fin y al cabo = after all. A fin de = in order to.
items.ex: Por fin llegó el fin de semana.
items.exEn: The weekend is finally here.

items.use: En el camino / de camino = on the way. Voy camino a casa = I'm on my way home. Usually a smaller road or path; a highway is carretera.
items.ex: Te llamo cuando esté en camino.
items.exEn: I'll call you when I'm on the way.

items.use: Los esposos = husband and wife, the couple. Esposas also means handcuffs.
items.ex: Mi esposo cocina los domingos.
items.exEn: My husband cooks on Sundays.

items.use: Hacer una pregunta = ask a question (not 'preguntar una pregunta'). A question to discuss is a cuestión or tema.
items.ex: ¿Puedo hacerte una pregunta?
items.exEn: Can I ask you a question?

items.use: Ends in -e and is feminine: la muerte. De muerte = intense or great (informal): un susto de muerte.
items.ex: La muerte de su abuelo fue muy dura.
items.exEn: His grandfather's death was very hard.

items.use: Use de before a noun: un millón de personas, dos millones de dólares. The accent drops in the plural: millones.
items.ex: Panamá tiene más de cuatro millones de habitantes.
items.exEn: Panama has more than four million inhabitants.

items.use: En realidad = actually, in fact. False friend: 'actualmente' means 'currently', so say en realidad for 'actually'.
items.ex: En realidad, no me gusta el café.
items.exEn: Actually, I don't like coffee.

items.use: Trabajo en equipo = teamwork. Singular verb: el equipo ganó. Also gear or equipment: equipo de buceo.
items.ex: ¿De qué equipo eres?
items.exEn: Which team do you support?

items.use: Pedir ayuda = ask for help. Necesito ayuda con... = I need help with... ¡Ayuda! = Help!
items.ex: Gracias por tu ayuda con la mudanza.
items.exEn: Thanks for your help with the move.

items.use: Me duele todo el cuerpo = my whole body aches. Can also mean a group or corps: cuerpo de bomberos (fire department).
items.ex: Después del gimnasio me duele todo el cuerpo.
items.exEn: After the gym my whole body hurts.

items.use: Jefe de... = head of: jefe de ventas. Informally ¡jefe! is a friendly way to address a man, e.g. a waiter or driver.
items.ex: Mi jefa me dio el viernes libre.
items.exEn: My boss gave me Friday off.

items.use: Use el before the title when talking about someone: el presidente Mulino. Female form: la presidenta is now standard.
items.ex: El presidente habló en la Asamblea.
items.exEn: The president spoke in the Assembly.

items.use: Singular verb: el gobierno anunció... Gobierno central = national government.
items.ex: El gobierno subió el precio de la gasolina.
items.exEn: The government raised the price of gas.

items.use: Un viejo can sound rude for an old person; un señor mayor or una persona mayor is polite. Mi viejo / mi vieja = my dad / my mom (affectionate).
items.ex: Mis viejos vienen a visitarnos en diciembre.
items.exEn: My folks are coming to visit us in December.
items.latam: 'Mi viejo / mi vieja' for parents is very common in Latin America. In Panama, 'mi vieja' can also mean 'my wife'.

items.use: La Tierra (capital T) = planet Earth. Por tierra = by land. Mi tierra = my homeland.
items.ex: Las plantas necesitan buena tierra.
items.exEn: Plants need good soil.

items.use: ¿Cuál es tu número (de teléfono)? Note: in Spanish, the noun for a big quantity is cantidad: una gran cantidad de gente.
items.ex: ¿Me das tu número de celular?
items.exEn: Can you give me your cell number?

items.use: El final = the end (of a movie, street, story). La final = the final match. Al final = in the end / at the end.
items.ex: Al final, decidimos quedarnos.
items.exEn: In the end, we decided to stay.

items.use: Trabajar en grupo = work in a group. Also a music band: un grupo de salsa. Grupo de WhatsApp is very common.
items.ex: Te agregué al grupo de la familia.
items.exEn: I added you to the family group chat.

items.use: Estar en guerra = be at war. Dar guerra = cause trouble (often about kids).
items.ex: Mi abuelo nunca hablaba de la guerra.
items.exEn: My grandfather never talked about the war.

items.use: Tenerle cariño a alguien = be fond of someone. Hacer cariño = pet, caress. Also used to address loved ones: cariño, ¿vienes?
items.ex: Le tengo mucho cariño a mi maestra.
items.exEn: I'm very fond of my teacher.

items.use: Dar clases = teach classes; tomar clases = take classes. Also 'kind': toda clase de... = all kinds of... Ends in -e, feminine.
items.ex: Tomo clases de español los martes.
items.exEn: I take Spanish lessons on Tuesdays.

items.use: Feminine but el arma in the singular (stressed a-): el arma, las armas. Arma de fuego = firearm.
items.ex: Está prohibido llevar armas en el avión.
items.exEn: It's forbidden to carry weapons on the plane.

items.use: Tener cara de... = look (tired, etc.): tienes cara de cansado. Cara a cara = face to face. As an adjective, cara means expensive.
items.ex: Tienes cara de no haber dormido.
items.exEn: You look like you didn't sleep.

items.use: Videojuego = video game. Juego de mesa = board game. Also a matching set: juego de sábanas. A sports match is usually partido.
items.ex: A mis hijos les encantan los juegos de mesa.
items.exEn: My kids love board games.

items.use: Use el / la when talking about them (la doctora Ruiz), no article when speaking to them (Buenos días, doctora). Ir al doctor = go to the doctor.
items.ex: Tengo cita con el doctor a las diez.
items.exEn: I have a doctor's appointment at ten.

items.use: De todo corazón = wholeheartedly. Also a term of affection: corazón, ven. The accent drops in the plural: corazones.
items.ex: Te lo agradezco de todo corazón.
items.exEn: I thank you with all my heart.

items.use: Tener suerte = be lucky. ¡Buena suerte! = good luck! Por suerte = luckily. Ends in -e, feminine.
items.ex: ¡Qué suerte que encontraste estacionamiento!
items.exEn: How lucky that you found parking!

items.use: False friend: a bookstore is una librería; a library is una biblioteca.
items.ex: Estoy leyendo un libro muy bueno.
items.exEn: I'm reading a very good book.

items.use: Plural changes z to c: luces. Prender / apagar la luz = turn the light on / off. Se fue la luz = the power went out. Dar a luz = give birth.
items.ex: Se fue la luz otra vez en el barrio.
items.exEn: The power went out again in the neighborhood.
items.latam: Latin America says 'prender la luz'; Spain says 'encender la luz'.

items.use: Tener miedo (de / a) = be afraid (of): tengo miedo a las culebras. Dar miedo = be scary: me da miedo manejar de noche.
items.ex: Me da miedo manejar con lluvia.
items.exEn: I'm scared of driving in the rain.

items.use: De todos modos = anyway. De modo que = so (that). Modo avión = airplane mode. Also grammar 'mood' (modo subjuntivo).
items.ex: De todos modos, te aviso mañana.
items.exEn: Anyway, I'll let you know tomorrow.

items.use: Words ending in -ción are feminine. Con relación a / en relación con = regarding. Tener una relación = be in a relationship.
items.ex: Tengo buena relación con mis compañeros.
items.exEn: I have a good relationship with my coworkers.

items.use: En cambio = on the other hand / instead. ¿Tiene cambio? = Do you have change? A cambio de = in exchange for.
items.ex: Yo prefiero la playa; mi esposa, en cambio, prefiere la montaña.
items.exEn: I prefer the beach; my wife, on the other hand, prefers the mountains.

items.use: Tener derecho a = have the right to. Estudiar derecho = study law. Derechos humanos = human rights. Don't confuse with derecha (right side).
items.ex: Todos tienen derecho a la educación.
items.exEn: Everyone has the right to education.

items.use: Hacer una prueba = take or give a test. A prueba de agua = waterproof. Also evidence: no hay pruebas.
items.ex: Mañana tengo una prueba de matemáticas.
items.exEn: Tomorrow I have a math test.

items.use: Tener sentido = make sense (not 'hacer sentido'). Sentido del humor = sense of humor. Calle de un solo sentido = one-way street.
items.ex: Eso no tiene sentido.
items.exEn: That doesn't make sense.

items.use: Gender changes the meaning: el orden = tidiness, sequence (en orden alfabético); la orden = a command (dar una orden). Plural gets an accent: órdenes.
items.ex: Me gusta tener la casa en orden.
items.exEn: I like to keep the house in order.
items.latam: In Latin America 'la orden' is also an order at a restaurant: ¿Ya tomaron su orden?

items.use: Sacar a pasear al perro = walk the dog. Perro caliente = hot dog. Careful: perra can be an insult for a woman.
items.ex: Saco al perro todas las mañanas.
items.exEn: I walk the dog every morning.

items.use: Dar una vuelta = go for a walk or ride. Darse la vuelta = turn around. De vuelta = back (estoy de vuelta). Ida y vuelta = round trip.
items.ex: Vamos a dar una vuelta por la Calzada de Amador.
items.exEn: Let's go for a walk along the Amador Causeway.

items.use: Mainly Spain's word for car. Learn it for the DELE, but use carro in Panama. Coche cama = sleeper car on a train.
items.ex: En Madrid casi no uso el coche.
items.exEn: In Madrid I hardly use the car.
items.latam: In Panama and most of Latin America say 'carro' (or 'auto' in the Southern Cone). In Panama 'coche' is often a baby stroller.

items.use: A la fuerza = by force / against your will. Hacer fuerza = push hard, make an effort. ¡Fuerza! = stay strong!
items.ex: No tengo fuerza para cargar esa caja.
items.exEn: I don't have the strength to carry that box.

items.use: Masculine though it ends in -a (Greek origin, like problema, tema, programa): el sistema. Se cayó el sistema = the system is down.
items.ex: El sistema del banco está caído.
items.exEn: The bank's system is down.

items.use: Paso a paso = step by step. Dar un paso = take a step. De paso = on the way / while at it. Estar de paso = be passing through.
items.ex: Vamos a hacerlo paso a paso.
items.exEn: Let's do it step by step.

items.use: ¿Qué planes tienes? = What are your plans? Hacer planes = make plans. Plan de datos = data plan (phone).
items.ex: ¿Tienes planes para el sábado?
items.exEn: Do you have plans for Saturday?

items.use: Ends in -e, feminine: la calle. En la calle = in the street / outside. Al otro lado de la calle = across the street.
items.ex: Vivo en la calle 50.
items.exEn: I live on 50th Street.

items.use: A small town, often in the countryside. El pueblo = the people of a nation: el pueblo panameño.
items.ex: Mi abuela vive en un pueblo de Los Santos.
items.exEn: My grandmother lives in a town in Los Santos.

items.use: Tener cuidado = be careful. ¡Cuidado! = Watch out! Cuidado con el perro = beware of the dog.
items.ex: Ten cuidado, el piso está mojado.
items.exEn: Be careful, the floor is wet.

items.use: A sports match: un partido de fútbol. Also a political party. A party with music is una fiesta, never un partido.
items.ex: ¿Vamos a ver el partido esta noche?
items.exEn: Shall we watch the game tonight?

items.use: Hacer una fiesta = throw a party. Ir de fiesta = go out partying. Las fiestas patrias = national holidays (in Panama, November).
items.ex: El sábado hacemos una fiesta en la casa.
items.exEn: On Saturday we're throwing a party at the house.

items.use: A pie = on foot (voy a pie). De pie = standing. Also the unit of length (foot).
items.ex: La tienda está cerca, podemos ir a pie.
items.exEn: The store is close, we can walk.

items.use: Gender changes the meaning: la frente = forehead; el frente = front (also a weather or war front). Frente a = in front of / facing.
items.ex: El hotel está frente al mar.
items.exEn: The hotel is facing the sea.

items.use: Usually primary or general school. Ir a la escuela = go to school. Colegio is also common for school (private or secondary).
items.ex: Mis hijos van a la escuela en bus.
items.exEn: My children go to school by bus.

items.use: Ends in -e, feminine: la sangre. Donar sangre = donate blood. Sangre fría = cool head, calm.
items.ex: Me sacaron sangre para unos exámenes.
items.exEn: They drew my blood for some tests.

items.use: Tener la oportunidad de + infinitive. Aprovechar la oportunidad = take the opportunity. Dar otra oportunidad = give another chance.
items.ex: Quiero aprovechar esta oportunidad para practicar.
items.exEn: I want to take this opportunity to practice.

items.use: Similar to chico; very common in Latin America. Muchachos also means 'guys' for a group.
items.ex: Ese muchacho trabaja en el supermercado.
items.exEn: That young man works at the supermarket.

items.use: Words ending in -ción are feminine. Estar en una situación difícil = be in a difficult situation.
items.ex: La situación del tráfico es terrible hoy.
items.exEn: The traffic situation is terrible today.

items.use: One word for both 'politics' and 'policy': la política nacional, la política de la empresa. A politician is un político / una política.
items.ex: No me gusta hablar de política.
items.exEn: I don't like talking about politics.

items.use: A specific law or the law in general. Plural: leyes. To study law is estudiar derecho, not 'ley'.
items.ex: La nueva ley entra en vigor en enero.
items.exEn: The new law comes into force in January.

items.use: Hablar por teléfono = talk on the phone. ¿Me das tu teléfono? = Can I have your number?
items.ex: Mi mamá está hablando por teléfono.
items.exEn: My mom is talking on the phone.
items.latam: For a mobile phone, Latin America says 'celular'; Spain says 'móvil'.

items.use: El servicio es bueno = the service is good. Servicio a domicilio = home delivery. Also a polite word for restroom: ¿Dónde está el servicio?
items.ex: El servicio en ese restaurante es muy lento.
items.exEn: The service at that restaurant is very slow.
items.latam: In Panama 'restroom' is usually 'el baño'. 'El servicio' for toilet is more Spain.

items.use: Covers boyfriend, fiancé and groom. Los novios = the couple, or bride and groom at a wedding.
items.ex: Mi hermana tiene novio nuevo.
items.exEn: My sister has a new boyfriend.

items.use: Puesto de trabajo = job position. Also a market stall: puesto de frutas. Primer puesto = first place.
items.ex: Solicité un puesto en el banco.
items.exEn: I applied for a position at the bank.

items.use: A memory of something (un buen recuerdo). A computer's memory is la memoria. Also a souvenir. Dale recuerdos a... = give my regards to...
items.ex: Compré unos recuerdos en el mercado de artesanías.
items.exEn: I bought some souvenirs at the craft market.

items.use: Cinturón de seguridad = seatbelt. Seguridad social = social security. Con seguridad = for sure. Also self-confidence.
items.ex: Ponte el cinturón de seguridad.
items.exEn: Put on your seatbelt.

items.use: Accent on dó in both forms: dólar, dólares. Cien dólares = one hundred dollars.
items.ex: El almuerzo cuesta ocho dólares.
items.exEn: Lunch costs eight dollars.
items.latam: Panama uses the US dollar, officially alongside the balboa. People also say 'un palo' informally for one dollar.

items.use: Obra de teatro = play. Obra de arte = work of art. Obras = roadworks or construction: hay obras en la calle.
items.ex: Fuimos a ver una obra de teatro en el Teatro Nacional.
items.exEn: We went to see a play at the National Theater.

items.use: Ver una película = watch a movie. Película de terror / de acción = horror / action movie. De película = amazing.
items.ex: ¿Quieres ver una película esta noche?
items.exEn: Do you want to watch a movie tonight?

items.use: Hacer una lista = make a list. Pasar lista = take attendance. Lista de espera = waiting list.
items.ex: Hice una lista de compras.
items.exEn: I made a shopping list.

items.use: Vino tinto = red wine (not 'rojo'); vino blanco = white wine. Also a form of the verb venir: él vino ayer.
items.ex: ¿Prefieres vino tinto o blanco?
items.exEn: Do you prefer red or white wine?

items.use: Ir al centro = go downtown. Centro comercial = shopping mall. En el centro de = in the middle of.
items.ex: Vamos al centro comercial a comprar zapatos.
items.exEn: Let's go to the mall to buy shoes.

items.use: No es asunto tuyo = it's none of your business. In an email, Asunto = Subject. Asuntos exteriores = foreign affairs.
items.ex: Tenemos que hablar de un asunto importante.
items.exEn: We need to talk about an important matter.

items.use: Uncountable, like in English: la información es correcta (not 'las informaciones' for 'pieces of information'). Pedir información = ask for information.
items.ex: Necesito más información sobre el curso.
items.exEn: I need more information about the course.

items.use: Common in hotels: una habitación doble. At home in Panama, people usually say cuarto for bedroom.
items.ex: Reservé una habitación con vista al mar.
items.exEn: I booked a room with an ocean view.

items.use: Hacer falta = be needed: me hace falta dinero. Sin falta = without fail. Falta de ortografía = spelling mistake. Also a foul in sports.
items.ex: No hace falta que vengas temprano.
items.exEn: There's no need for you to come early.

items.use: El cielo está despejado = the sky is clear. Also heaven. Mi cielo is a term of affection (darling).
items.ex: Hoy el cielo está muy nublado.
items.exEn: The sky is very cloudy today.

items.use: Hombre / mujer de negocios = businessman / businesswoman. Viaje de negocios = business trip. Hacer negocio = do business, make a deal.
items.ex: Mi tío tiene un negocio de comida en El Cangrejo.
items.exEn: My uncle has a food business in El Cangrejo.

items.use: Tener sueño = be sleepy (not 'estar dormido'). Also a dream: mi sueño es viajar. Tener un sueño = have a dream.
items.ex: Tengo mucho sueño, me voy a acostar.
items.exEn: I'm really sleepy, I'm going to bed.

items.use: Of a ship, plane, team or army. The accent drops in the plural: capitanes.
items.ex: El capitán del barco nos dio la bienvenida.
items.exEn: The ship's captain welcomed us.

items.use: Comida rápida = fast food. Also a meal: tres comidas al día.
items.ex: La comida panameña es deliciosa.
items.exEn: Panamanian food is delicious.
items.latam: In Spain 'la comida' is the main midday meal (lunch). In Latin America lunch is 'el almuerzo', and 'la comida' can be dinner in some countries.

items.use: El bebé for a boy or unknown sex, la bebé for a girl. Esperar un bebé = be expecting a baby.
items.ex: Mi prima va a tener un bebé en marzo.
items.exEn: My cousin is having a baby in March.

items.use: Plural changes z to c: voces. En voz alta = aloud, out loud; en voz baja = quietly. Mensaje de voz = voice message.
items.ex: Lee el texto en voz alta, por favor.
items.exEn: Read the text out loud, please.

items.use: Ends in -o but is feminine (short for la fotografía): la foto, las fotos. Tomar una foto = take a photo.
items.ex: ¿Nos tomas una foto, por favor?
items.exEn: Could you take a photo of us, please?
items.latam: Latin America says 'tomar una foto'; Spain usually says 'hacer una foto'.

items.use: Un par de = a pair of (un par de zapatos), and often 'a couple of, a few': un par de días. Abierto de par en par = wide open.
items.ex: Vuelvo en un par de días.
items.exEn: I'll be back in a couple of days.

items.use: Feminine: la paz. Déjame en paz = leave me alone. Hacer las paces = make up (after a fight).
items.ex: ¡Déjame en paz, estoy trabajando!
items.exEn: Leave me alone, I'm working!

items.use: Tener la culpa = be to blame. Es mi culpa = it's my fault. Echarle la culpa a alguien = blame someone. Por tu culpa = because of you.
items.ex: No es tu culpa, no te preocupes.
items.exEn: It's not your fault, don't worry.

items.use: Countable, unlike English 'news': una buena noticia = a piece of good news. Las noticias = the news (on TV).
items.ex: Tengo una buena noticia: ¡me dieron el trabajo!
items.exEn: I have good news: I got the job!

items.use: Uncountable: me gusta la música. Escuchar música = listen to music. A musician is un músico / una música.
items.ex: Siempre escucho música en el carro.
items.exEn: I always listen to music in the car.

items.use: Common in exclamations: ¿Qué diablos...? = What the heck...? Pobre diablo = poor guy. Mildly informal, not vulgar.
items.ex: ¿Dónde diablos dejé las llaves?
items.exEn: Where the heck did I leave my keys?
items.latam: In Panama the 'diablicos' are traditional devil dancers seen at festivals like Corpus Christi.

items.use: El resto de = the rest of: el resto del día. Restos = remains or leftovers.
items.ex: Pasé el resto del día en la playa.
items.exEn: I spent the rest of the day at the beach.

items.use: Ir al médico = go to the doctor. As an adjective: cita médica (medical appointment), seguro médico (health insurance).
items.ex: Tengo que ir al médico mañana.
items.exEn: I have to go to the doctor tomorrow.

items.use: Escribir una carta = write a letter. Jugar a las cartas = play cards. La carta = the restaurant menu. False friend: a greeting card is una tarjeta.
items.ex: ¿Nos trae la carta, por favor?
items.exEn: Could you bring us the menu, please?
items.latam: In Latin American restaurants 'el menú' is more common than 'la carta'.

items.use: Don / doña go before a first name to show respect: don Pedro, doña Carmen. Also a natural talent: tiene un don para la música.
items.ex: Doña Rosa vende las mejores empanadas del barrio.
items.exEn: Doña Rosa sells the best empanadas in the neighborhood.
items.latam: Very common in Panama and Latin America for older people, neighbors and shop owners.

items.use: Masculine though it ends in -a: el programa. Un programa de televisión = a TV show. Also software or a course of study.
items.ex: Mi programa favorito empieza a las ocho.
items.exEn: My favorite show starts at eight.

items.use: Sitio web = website. A place in general: un sitio tranquilo.
items.ex: Conozco un sitio muy bueno para comer mariscos.
items.exEn: I know a really good place to eat seafood.
items.latam: Spain uses 'sitio' for 'place' much more. In Panama 'lugar' is more common.

items.use: El campo = the countryside (as opposed to the city). Also a sports field and an area of study (campo de la medicina).
items.ex: Los fines de semana vamos al campo.
items.exEn: On weekends we go to the countryside.
items.latam: In Panama, the countryside and rural interior are often called 'el interior'.

items.use: Irse a la cama = go to bed. Hacer la cama = make the bed. Estar en cama = be sick in bed.
items.ex: Todos los días hago la cama.
items.exEn: I make the bed every day.

items.use: Los abuelos = grandparents (both). Also used kindly for elderly people.
items.ex: Los domingos almorzamos con los abuelos.
items.exEn: On Sundays we have lunch with my grandparents.

items.use: Ends in -e, masculine: el viaje. Hacer un viaje = take a trip. ¡Buen viaje! = Have a good trip! Estar de viaje = be away on a trip.
items.ex: ¡Buen viaje! Avísame cuando llegues.
items.exEn: Have a good trip! Let me know when you arrive.

items.use: Like diablo, used in exclamations: ¿Qué demonios pasa aquí? = What on earth is going on here?
items.ex: ¿Qué demonios estás haciendo?
items.exEn: What on earth are you doing?

items.use: Ir a la oficina = go to the office. Trabajar desde casa = work from home. Oficina de correos = post office.
items.ex: Hoy trabajo desde casa, no voy a la oficina.
items.exEn: Today I'm working from home, I'm not going to the office.

items.use: Película de acción = action movie. Una buena acción = a good deed. In business, acciones = shares.
items.ex: Me encantan las películas de acción.
items.exEn: I love action movies.

items.use: En línea = online. Línea del metro = metro line. Mantener la línea = stay slim. Keep the accent: línea.
items.ex: Puedes pagar la luz en línea.
items.exEn: You can pay the electricity bill online.

items.use: Same form for both: el agente / la agente. Agente de viajes = travel agent. Agente de policía = police officer.
items.ex: Un agente de tránsito nos detuvo.
items.exEn: A traffic officer stopped us.

items.use: Uncountable for the material: papel. Una hoja de papel = a sheet of paper. Papel higiénico = toilet paper. Hacer un papel = play a role.
items.ex: Se acabó el papel higiénico.
items.exEn: We ran out of toilet paper.

items.use: Ends in -e, masculine: el aire. Aire acondicionado = air conditioning. Al aire libre = outdoors.
items.ex: Prende el aire, que hace mucho calor.
items.exEn: Turn on the AC, it's really hot.
items.latam: In Panama 'el aire' alone means the air conditioning.

items.use: Al principio = at first. A principios de = at the beginning of (a principios de mayo). Also a moral principle: una persona de principios.
items.ex: Al principio no entendía nada.
items.exEn: At first I didn't understand anything.

items.use: The usual word for a company. Trabajar en una empresa = work for a company. Empresa privada = private company.
items.ex: Trabajo en una empresa de logística.
items.exEn: I work for a logistics company.

items.use: The head of a company, a film, an orchestra, or a school principal: el director de la escuela.
items.ex: La directora de la escuela llamó a los padres.
items.exEn: The school principal called the parents.

items.use: Por ejemplo = for example (abbreviated p. ej.). Dar un ejemplo = give an example; dar el ejemplo = set an example.
items.ex: ¿Me puedes dar un ejemplo?
items.exEn: Can you give me an example?

items.use: Los reyes = the king and queen. Día de Reyes (6 January) = Epiphany, the day of the Three Kings.
items.ex: El rey de España visitó Panamá.
items.exEn: The king of Spain visited Panama.

items.use: Means a room, often a bedroom. Also 'a quarter' in time: las dos y cuarto (2:15), un cuarto de hora (15 minutes).
items.ex: Mi cuarto es pequeño pero tiene aire.
items.exEn: My bedroom is small but it has AC.
items.latam: In Panama 'cuarto' is the usual word for bedroom; Spain prefers 'dormitorio' or 'habitación'.

items.use: Tomar una decisión = make a decision (not 'hacer'). The accent drops in the plural: decisiones.
items.ex: Tengo que tomar una decisión hoy.
items.exEn: I have to make a decision today.

items.use: Perder el control = lose control. Control remoto = remote control. Control de seguridad = security check.
items.ex: ¿Dónde está el control del televisor?
items.exEn: Where's the TV remote?

items.use: Estar en el hospital = be in the hospital. Ir al hospital. The h is silent.
items.ex: Llevaron a mi abuelo al hospital.
items.exEn: They took my grandfather to the hospital.

items.use: Same meaning as esposo; esposo is more neutral in Latin America. There is no feminine form: wife is esposa or mujer.
items.ex: Su marido es ingeniero.
items.exEn: Her husband is an engineer.

items.use: Fuegos artificiales = fireworks. A fuego lento = on low heat. A building fire is usually un incendio.
items.ex: Cocina el arroz a fuego lento.
items.exEn: Cook the rice on low heat.

items.use: Masculine though it ends in -a: el tema. Cambiar de tema = change the subject. Also a song: un tema nuevo.
items.ex: Mejor cambiemos de tema.
items.exEn: Let's change the subject.

items.use: Dar una respuesta = give an answer. En respuesta a = in reply to. Sin respuesta = unanswered.
items.ex: Todavía no tengo respuesta del banco.
items.exEn: I still don't have an answer from the bank.

items.use: Nivel de español = Spanish level. A nivel del mar = at sea level. Ends in -l, masculine.
items.ex: Mi nivel de español es B1.
items.exEn: My Spanish level is B1.

items.use: Estudios = studies, education: terminar los estudios. Also a research study, a studio (TV, recording) or a small apartment.
items.ex: Terminó sus estudios en la Universidad de Panamá.
items.exEn: She finished her studies at the University of Panama.

items.use: Guardar un secreto = keep a secret. En secreto = secretly.
items.ex: ¿Puedes guardar un secreto?
items.exEn: Can you keep a secret?

items.use: Ends in -e, masculine: el mensaje. Mandar un mensaje = send a text. Dejar un mensaje = leave a message.
items.ex: Te mando un mensaje cuando llegue.
items.exEn: I'll text you when I arrive.

items.use: Dar resultado = work, be effective. Los resultados del examen = exam results. Also a match score.
items.ex: Mañana me dan los resultados del examen.
items.exEn: Tomorrow they give me the test results.

items.use: Cometer un error = make a mistake (not 'hacer un error'). Por error = by mistake.
items.ex: Cometí un error en la factura.
items.exEn: I made a mistake on the invoice.

items.use: En el futuro = in the future. Also the grammar tense: el futuro (hablaré).
items.ex: En el futuro quiero vivir cerca de la playa.
items.exEn: In the future I want to live near the beach.

items.use: Add the context: compañero de clase (classmate), de trabajo (coworker), de cuarto (roommate). Also a partner.
items.ex: Almuerzo con mis compañeros de trabajo.
items.exEn: I have lunch with my coworkers.

items.use: Prestar atención = pay attention (not 'pagar'). Llamar la atención = attract attention, or scold. Atención al cliente = customer service.
items.ex: Presten atención, por favor.
items.exEn: Please pay attention.

items.use: Common in 'zona de comida', 'zona libre', 'zona rural'. Feminine: la zona.
items.ex: Vivimos en una zona tranquila de la ciudad.
items.exEn: We live in a quiet area of the city.
items.latam: In Panama, 'Zona Libre de Colón' is the famous free-trade zone; older people say 'la Zona' for the former Canal Zone.

items.use: 'Tener buena vista' = have good eyesight. 'Con vista al mar' = with a sea view. 'Hasta la vista' = see you.
items.ex: El apartamento tiene una vista increíble al mar.
items.exEn: The apartment has an amazing view of the sea.

items.use: Ask age with '¿Qué edad tiene?' or '¿Cuántos años tiene?'. 'Mayor de edad' = adult (18+).
items.ex: ¿Qué edad tiene tu hijo?
items.exEn: How old is your son?

items.use: Use 'abogada' for a woman. 'Contratar a un abogado' = hire a lawyer.
items.ex: Necesito hablar con mi abogado antes de firmar.
items.exEn: I need to talk to my lawyer before signing.

items.use: Means both a street address and a direction. 'En dirección a' = heading toward. Also the management of a company.
items.ex: ¿Me das tu dirección para mandarte el paquete?
items.exEn: Can you give me your address to send you the package?
items.latam: Panama addresses use landmarks more than numbers: 'del Super 99, dos casas a la derecha'.

items.use: 'Al fondo' = at the back/end. 'En el fondo' = deep down. 'Fondos' = funds (money).
items.ex: El baño está al fondo, a la derecha.
items.exEn: The bathroom is at the back, on the right.

items.use: Old-fashioned; often negative (a spoiled, idle rich young man). The feminine 'señorita' is very common: 'Miss', young woman.
items.ex: Se comporta como un señorito que nunca ha trabajado.
items.exEn: He acts like a spoiled rich kid who has never worked.
items.latam: 'Señorito' is mostly heard in Spain. In Panama 'señorita' is used daily to address a young woman or a female teacher.

items.use: Both a business and keeping someone company: 'hacerle compañía a alguien'. Note the accent on í.
items.ex: Trabajo para una compañía de seguros.
items.exEn: I work for an insurance company.
items.latam: In Panama 'empresa' is also very common for a business.

items.use: 'Estar en proceso' = be in progress. In law, 'un proceso judicial' is a trial.
items.ex: El proceso para sacar la visa es muy lento.
items.exEn: The process to get the visa is very slow.

items.use: Covers both academic research and police investigations. 'Hacer una investigación sobre...'.
items.ex: La policía abrió una investigación sobre el robo.
items.exEn: The police opened an investigation into the robbery.

items.use: Both the drink and the place. 'Café con leche', 'café negro'. As an adjective it means brown (ojos café).
items.ex: ¿Quieres un café antes de irnos?
items.exEn: Do you want a coffee before we go?
items.latam: Panama is famous for its Geisha coffee from Boquete. 'Ojos café' (brown eyes) is common in LatAm; Spain prefers 'marrones'.

items.use: 'Tener una duda' = have a question. 'Sin duda' = without a doubt. 'No cabe duda' = there is no doubt.
items.ex: Si tienen alguna duda, me escriben.
items.exEn: If you have any questions, message me.

items.use: Capital 'Estado' = the government/nation. 'Estado civil' = marital status. 'En buen estado' = in good condition.
items.ex: El carro está en buen estado.
items.exEn: The car is in good condition.

items.use: Uncountable singular: 'la ropa' = clothes. Do not say 'las ropas' for everyday clothes. 'Ropa interior' = underwear.
items.ex: Tengo que lavar la ropa hoy.
items.exEn: I have to wash the clothes today.

items.use: 'Valor' = value/worth and also courage (tener valor). 'Valores' = moral values.
items.ex: Hace falta mucho valor para decir la verdad.
items.exEn: It takes a lot of courage to tell the truth.

items.use: Used for teachers at any level, not only university. Address as 'profe' informally.
items.ex: La profesora nos dejó mucha tarea.
items.exEn: The teacher gave us a lot of homework.
items.latam: In Panama students often say 'profe' or 'teacher' (even in Spanish) to their teacher.

items.use: Work meetings and social gatherings. 'Tener una reunión' = have a meeting.
items.ex: Tengo una reunión a las tres.
items.exEn: I have a meeting at three.

items.use: 'Boca arriba / boca abajo' = face up / face down. 'Boca del metro' = subway entrance.
items.ex: Abre la boca, por favor.
items.exEn: Open your mouth, please.
items.latam: Bocas del Toro is a well-known province and island group in Panama.

items.use: Camera, and also a legislative chamber ('Cámara de Comercio'). Stress on the first syllable: CÁ-ma-ra.
items.ex: Hay cámaras de seguridad en la entrada.
items.exEn: There are security cameras at the entrance.

items.use: 'No hay espacio' = there is no room. Also outer space and a time slot.
items.ex: No hay espacio para otra cama en el cuarto.
items.exEn: There is no room for another bed in the bedroom.

items.use: Feminine: la imagen. Plural adds an accent: imágenes. Also public image: 'cuidar la imagen'.
items.ex: Mándame la imagen por WhatsApp.
items.exEn: Send me the picture on WhatsApp.

items.use: 'Estar a cargo de' = be in charge of. 'Cargo' = job position. Also a bank charge or legal charge.
items.ex: Ella está a cargo del proyecto.
items.exEn: She is in charge of the project.

items.use: Polite word for a man: 'Damas y caballeros'. On restroom doors: 'Caballeros'. Feminine counterpart is 'dama'.
items.ex: Disculpe, caballero, ¿esta silla está libre?
items.exEn: Excuse me, sir, is this seat free?

items.use: 'Existe la posibilidad de que...' takes the subjunctive.
items.ex: Hay posibilidad de que llueva esta tarde.
items.exEn: There's a chance it will rain this afternoon.

items.use: Use for any college or university. 'Ir a la universidad' or informally 'la U'.
items.ex: Mi hermana estudia en la universidad.
items.exEn: My sister studies at the university.
items.latam: In Panama, people say 'la U' and often mean the Universidad de Panamá.

items.use: One 'consejo' = one piece of advice; 'consejos' = advice. 'Dar un consejo'. Also a council or board.
items.ex: Te voy a dar un consejo: ahorra desde ahora.
items.exEn: I'll give you some advice: start saving now.

items.use: Any killer, not only of politicians. Also used as an adjective.
items.ex: La policía todavía busca al asesino.
items.exEn: The police are still looking for the killer.

items.use: 'Hacer daño' = to hurt. 'Me hace daño' = it hurts me / it's bad for me. 'Daños' = damage (to things).
items.ex: El huracán causó muchos daños.
items.exEn: The hurricane caused a lot of damage.

items.use: Society in general, and also a company: 'sociedad anónima (S.A.)'.
items.ex: Vivimos en una sociedad muy conectada.
items.exEn: We live in a very connected society.
items.latam: Panamanian company names often end in 'S.A.' (sociedad anónima).

items.use: 'A base de' = based on / made from. 'Base de datos' = database.
items.ex: Esta salsa está hecha a base de tomate.
items.exEn: This sauce is made with a tomato base.

items.use: 'Tener un proyecto' = have a plan. 'Proyecto de ley' = bill (law).
items.ex: Estamos trabajando en un proyecto nuevo.
items.exEn: We are working on a new project.

items.use: 'Poner la mesa' = set the table. 'Recoger la mesa' = clear the table. 'Mesa de noche' = nightstand.
items.ex: ¿Me ayudas a poner la mesa?
items.exEn: Can you help me set the table?

items.use: Same form for both: el paciente / la paciente. Also an adjective: 'ser paciente' = be patient.
items.ex: El doctor está atendiendo a otro paciente.
items.exEn: The doctor is seeing another patient.

items.use: Physical movement and social/political movements. Also bank transactions: 'movimientos de la cuenta'.
items.ex: No hagas movimientos bruscos.
items.exEn: Don't make sudden movements.

items.use: Usually a primary school teacher. Also a master of a craft ('maestro de obras' = foreman).
items.ex: La maestra de mi hijo es muy buena.
items.exEn: My son's teacher is very good.
items.latam: In Panama 'maestro' also refers to a builder or handyman: 'el maestro viene a arreglar el techo'.

items.use: False friend: 'carrera' is usually your degree course ('¿Qué carrera estudias?'), plus a race.
items.ex: Estudio la carrera de Derecho.
items.exEn: I'm studying for a law degree.

items.use: 'Montar a caballo' = ride a horse. Also the knight in chess.
items.ex: Los domingos montamos a caballo en el campo.
items.exEn: On Sundays we go horseback riding in the countryside.

items.use: Spanish uses Roman numerals: 'siglo XXI' (veintiuno). 'Hace siglos' = for ages.
items.ex: Este edificio es del siglo XIX.
items.exEn: This building is from the 19th century.

items.use: As a word on its own: 'Perdón' = sorry / excuse me. 'Pedir perdón' = apologize.
items.ex: Perdón, no te vi.
items.exEn: Sorry, I didn't see you.

items.use: '¡Qué pena!' = what a shame. 'Vale la pena' = it's worth it. 'Pena de muerte' = death penalty.
items.ex: Vale la pena visitar el Casco Viejo.
items.exEn: It's worth visiting the Casco Viejo.
items.latam: In Panama and much of LatAm 'me da pena' means 'I'm embarrassed/shy'. In Spain it means 'I feel sorry'.

items.use: Both a bank and a bench (seat in a park).
items.ex: Voy al banco a depositar un cheque.
items.exEn: I'm going to the bank to deposit a check.

items.use: 'La mayoría de' + noun = most. The verb can be singular or plural: 'La mayoría de la gente piensa...'.
items.ex: La mayoría de mis amigos trabaja en la ciudad.
items.exEn: Most of my friends work in the city.

items.use: Same form for women: 'ella es miembro' (also 'miembra' in some media). Also a limb of the body.
items.ex: Es miembro del club desde hace años.
items.exEn: He has been a member of the club for years.

items.use: 'En buenas condiciones' = in good condition. 'Con la condición de que' + subjunctive = on condition that.
items.ex: Te lo presto con la condición de que me lo devuelvas.
items.exEn: I'll lend it to you on condition that you give it back.

items.use: 'En efecto' = indeed. 'Efectos secundarios' = side effects.
items.ex: Este medicamento no tiene efectos secundarios.
items.exEn: This medicine has no side effects.

items.use: 'Con los brazos abiertos' = with open arms. 'Del brazo' = arm in arm.
items.ex: Me duele el brazo derecho.
items.exEn: My right arm hurts.

items.use: A government minister, not a priest. 'Primer ministro' = prime minister.
items.ex: La ministra de Salud dio una conferencia.
items.exEn: The Health Minister gave a press conference.

items.use: 'Libertad de expresión' = freedom of speech. 'Tomarse la libertad de...' = take the liberty of.
items.ex: Aquí tienes libertad para decir lo que piensas.
items.exEn: Here you're free to say what you think.

items.use: Any murder, not only of a famous person.
items.ex: El asesinato ocurrió anoche cerca del puerto.
items.exEn: The murder happened last night near the port.

items.use: Both curiosity and money interest. 'Tener interés en' = be interested in. Plural loses the accent: intereses.
items.ex: El banco cobra un interés muy alto.
items.exEn: The bank charges very high interest.

items.use: Masculine even for female animals: el animal. 'Animal' is also an insult for a rough person.
items.ex: ¿Te gustan los animales?
items.exEn: Do you like animals?

items.use: 'Hace sol' = it's sunny. 'Tomar el sol' = sunbathe. 'Al sol' = in the sun.
items.ex: Hoy hace mucho sol, ponte bloqueador.
items.exEn: It's very sunny today, put on sunscreen.
items.latam: In Panama sunscreen is usually called 'bloqueador'.

items.use: Masculine: el color. Ask '¿De qué color es?' = What color is it?
items.ex: ¿De qué color es tu carro?
items.exEn: What color is your car?

items.use: 'Caja' = box, and also the checkout in a store: 'pagar en caja'.
items.ex: Puede pagar en la caja número tres.
items.exEn: You can pay at checkout number three.
items.latam: 'Caja de Seguro Social' (la Caja, CSS) is Panama's public health and pension system.

items.use: El cliente / la cliente; 'la clienta' is also very common. 'Atención al cliente' = customer service.
items.ex: El cliente siempre tiene la razón.
items.exEn: The customer is always right.

items.use: Always feminine, even for a man: 'Él fue la víctima'.
items.ex: Él fue víctima de un robo en el bus.
items.exEn: He was the victim of a robbery on the bus.

items.use: 'Pedir un deseo' = make a wish. 'Mis mejores deseos' = my best wishes.
items.ex: Pide un deseo antes de soplar las velas.
items.exEn: Make a wish before you blow out the candles.

items.use: Masculine in the singular (el arte moderno) but often feminine in the plural (las bellas artes).
items.ex: Me encanta el arte moderno.
items.exEn: I love modern art.

items.use: 'A causa de' = because of. Also a cause you support and a legal case.
items.ex: El vuelo se canceló a causa del mal tiempo.
items.exEn: The flight was cancelled because of bad weather.

items.use: 'Tengo cita con el médico' = doctor's appointment. 'Una cita' can also be a romantic date.
items.ex: Tengo cita con el dentista el lunes.
items.exEn: I have a dentist appointment on Monday.

items.use: '¡Trato hecho!' = it's a deal! 'Buen trato' = good treatment of people.
items.ex: Te doy cincuenta dólares. ¿Trato hecho?
items.exEn: I'll give you fifty dollars. Deal?

items.use: The h is silent. 'Hospedarse en un hotel' = stay at a hotel.
items.ex: Nos quedamos en un hotel cerca de la playa.
items.exEn: We stayed at a hotel near the beach.

items.use: Stars in the sky and famous people: 'una estrella de cine'. 'Hotel de cinco estrellas'.
items.ex: Esta noche se ven muchas estrellas.
items.exEn: You can see a lot of stars tonight.

items.use: On forms, 'sexo' means male or female. Neutral word in official use.
items.ex: Escriba su nombre, edad y sexo en el formulario.
items.exEn: Write your name, age and sex on the form.

items.use: Masculine: el dolor. 'Dolor de cabeza' = headache. 'Tengo dolor de...' or 'Me duele...'.
items.ex: Tengo un dolor de cabeza terrible.
items.exEn: I have a terrible headache.

items.use: 'La mitad de' + noun. 'A mitad de precio' = half price. 'En la mitad' = in the middle.
items.ex: Me comí la mitad de la pizza.
items.exEn: I ate half of the pizza.

items.use: 'Mucho gusto' = nice to meet you. 'Con gusto' = with pleasure. 'A gusto' = comfortable.
items.ex: Mucho gusto, me llamo Ana.
items.exEn: Nice to meet you, my name is Ana.
items.latam: In Panama 'con gusto' is the usual reply to 'gracias' in shops.

items.use: Feminine: la canción. Plural loses the accent: canciones.
items.ex: Esa canción suena en todas las fiestas.
items.exEn: That song plays at every party.

items.use: '¿Dónde está el baño?' = where's the restroom? 'Darse un baño' = take a bath; also a swim.
items.ex: Disculpe, ¿dónde está el baño?
items.exEn: Excuse me, where is the restroom?

items.use: 'Cumplir un objetivo' = reach a goal. Also a camera lens.
items.ex: Nuestro objetivo es terminar en marzo.
items.exEn: Our goal is to finish in March.

items.use: Almost always in set phrases: 'con respecto a' = regarding; 'al respecto' = about it. Do not confuse with 'respeto' (respect for someone).
items.ex: ¿Qué opinas al respecto?
items.exEn: What do you think about it?

items.use: '¡Salud!' = cheers! and 'bless you' after a sneeze. Feminine: la salud.
items.ex: Lo más importante es la salud.
items.exEn: Health is the most important thing.

items.use: Feminine: la sal. 'Pásame la sal' = pass me the salt.
items.ex: A la sopa le falta sal.
items.exEn: The soup needs more salt.
items.latam: In parts of LatAm (Panama, Colombia), 'qué sal' can mean 'what bad luck'.

items.use: 'Tener en mente' = keep in mind. 'Se me fue de la mente' = it slipped my mind.
items.ex: Tengo en mente un viaje a Boquete.
items.exEn: I have a trip to Boquete in mind.

items.use: 'En el suelo' = on the floor/ground. Also the soil for plants.
items.ex: Se me cayó el celular al suelo.
items.exEn: My phone fell on the floor.
items.latam: In Panama 'piso' is more common for the floor inside a house.

items.use: Physical position, rank, or point of view: 'Mi posición es clara'.
items.ex: ¿Cuál es tu posición sobre este tema?
items.exEn: What is your position on this issue?

items.use: 'Tomar medidas' = take measures (action) or measurements. 'A medida que' = as (over time). 'Hecho a la medida' = custom-made.
items.ex: El gobierno tomó medidas contra la inflación.
items.exEn: The government took measures against inflation.

items.use: Always ends in -e, singular and plural: 'una especie', 'las especies'. 'Una especie de' = a kind of.
items.ex: Panamá tiene muchas especies de aves.
items.exEn: Panama has many species of birds.

items.use: 'La diferencia entre A y B'. 'A diferencia de' = unlike.
items.ex: ¿Cuál es la diferencia entre estos dos modelos?
items.exEn: What's the difference between these two models?

items.use: '¿Qué precio tiene?' = what's the price? 'Subir/bajar los precios'.
items.ex: Los precios en el súper subieron mucho.
items.exEn: Prices at the supermarket went up a lot.

items.use: 'El pelo' = all the hair on your head (singular). Also animal fur. 'Cortarse el pelo' = get a haircut.
items.ex: Mañana me voy a cortar el pelo.
items.exEn: Tomorrow I'm going to get a haircut.
items.latam: 'Cabello' is a more formal synonym.

items.use: 'En mi opinión' = in my opinion. 'Cambiar de opinión' = change your mind.
items.ex: Cambié de opinión, mejor vamos mañana.
items.exEn: I changed my mind, let's go tomorrow instead.

items.use: A place to buy food and also the economic market: 'el mercado laboral'.
items.ex: Compramos pescado fresco en el mercado.
items.exEn: We buy fresh fish at the market.
items.latam: Panama City's 'Mercado de Mariscos' is the famous seafood market.

items.use: 'Las elecciones' (plural) = elections. Singular often means a choice.
items.ex: Las elecciones son en mayo.
items.exEn: The elections are in May.

items.use: 'En el interior' = inside. 'Ropa interior' = underwear. 'El interior del país' = the provinces.
items.ex: El interior de la casa es muy moderno.
items.exEn: The inside of the house is very modern.
items.latam: In Panama 'el interior' means the provinces outside Panama City: 'me voy pal interior'.

items.use: '¡Silencio!' = quiet! 'En silencio' = in silence. 'Guardar silencio' = keep quiet.
items.ex: Por favor, guarden silencio en la biblioteca.
items.exEn: Please keep quiet in the library.

items.use: 'No hay necesidad de...' = there's no need to. 'Hacer sus necesidades' = go to the toilet (polite).
items.ex: No hay necesidad de gritar.
items.exEn: There's no need to shout.

items.use: The noun 'el odio'. Do not confuse with 'odio' = I hate (verb).
items.ex: El odio no resuelve nada.
items.exEn: Hatred doesn't solve anything.

items.use: Work experience and life experiences: 'tener experiencia en ventas'.
items.ex: ¿Tienes experiencia en atención al cliente?
items.exEn: Do you have experience in customer service?

items.use: 'Actividades al aire libre' = outdoor activities. 'Actividad física' = exercise.
items.ex: El hotel ofrece muchas actividades para niños.
items.exEn: The hotel offers many activities for children.

items.use: Usually illegal drugs. For medicine, say 'medicamento' or 'medicina'.
items.ex: La policía encontró drogas en el barco.
items.exEn: The police found drugs on the boat.
items.latam: False friend: a pharmacy is 'farmacia', and medicine is 'medicina', never 'droga'.

items.use: 'Tener un accidente' = have an accident. 'Por accidente' = by accident.
items.ex: Hubo un accidente en el Corredor Sur.
items.exEn: There was an accident on the Corredor Sur.

items.use: Plural 'clubes' (also 'clubs'). 'Club de fútbol', 'club de lectura'.
items.ex: Me inscribí en un club de lectura.
items.exEn: I joined a book club.

items.use: Stress on the second syllable: e-JÉR-ci-to.
items.ex: Su abuelo sirvió en el ejército.
items.exEn: His grandfather served in the army.
items.latam: Panama has no army since 1990; it has a national police force (Fuerza Pública).

items.use: Usually masculine: el mar. 'La mar' appears in poetry and among fishermen. 'Alta mar' = open sea.
items.ex: Me encanta nadar en el mar.
items.exEn: I love swimming in the sea.

items.use: 'Ataque al corazón' = heart attack. 'Ataque de risa' = laughing fit.
items.ex: Le dio un ataque de risa en plena reunión.
items.exEn: He got a laughing fit in the middle of the meeting.

items.use: 'Estar en contacto' = be in touch. 'Ponerse en contacto con' = get in touch with. Also a phone contact.
items.ex: Seguimos en contacto por correo.
items.exEn: Let's stay in touch by email.

items.use: Feminine but takes 'el' in the singular: el alma, las almas. Adjectives stay feminine: el alma buena.
items.ex: Lo siento con toda el alma.
items.exEn: I'm deeply sorry.

items.use: El soldado / la soldado (some also say 'la soldada').
items.ex: El soldado regresó a casa después de un año.
items.exEn: The soldier came home after a year.

items.use: Key for a lock. In LatAm also the faucet/tap: 'abre la llave'.
items.ex: No encuentro las llaves del carro.
items.exEn: I can't find the car keys.
items.latam: In Panama 'la pluma' is also used for the faucet; in Spain it's 'el grifo'.

items.use: Personal energy and power: 'energía solar'. 'Se fue la energía' = the power went out.
items.ex: Hoy no tengo energía para nada.
items.exEn: Today I have no energy for anything.
items.latam: In Panama people say 'se fue la luz' when the power goes out.

items.use: General word for a boat or ship. 'En barco' = by boat.
items.ex: Los barcos esperan para cruzar el Canal.
items.exEn: The ships are waiting to cross the Canal.

items.use: Women: 'la jueza' (most common) or 'la juez'. Plural: jueces. Also a sports referee.
items.ex: La jueza dictó sentencia ayer.
items.exEn: The judge passed sentence yesterday.

items.use: Accent on í. 'A orillas del río' = on the riverbank.
items.ex: Nos bañamos en el río el domingo.
items.exEn: We swam in the river on Sunday.

items.use: Store in general; 'tienda de campaña' = tent.
items.ex: Hay una tienda de ropa en la esquina.
items.exEn: There's a clothing store on the corner.
items.latam: For a small corner shop, Panamanians often say 'el chino' or 'la tiendita'.

items.use: 'En avión' = by plane. Plural loses the accent: aviones.
items.ex: El avión sale a las seis de la mañana.
items.exEn: The plane leaves at six in the morning.

items.use: As a noun, 'dulces' = candy/sweets. As an adjective, 'dulce' = sweet.
items.ex: Los niños comieron muchos dulces en la fiesta.
items.exEn: The kids ate lots of candy at the party.
items.latam: In LatAm 'dulce' is the usual word for candy; Spain says 'caramelos' or 'chuches'.

items.use: Surgery, a math operation, or a police/military operation.
items.ex: La operación salió bien.
items.exEn: The surgery went well.

items.use: A meeting (often by chance) or an event. Also a sports match.
items.ex: Fue un encuentro inesperado en el aeropuerto.
items.exEn: It was an unexpected encounter at the airport.

items.use: Source of information ('fuentes oficiales') or of water. Also a serving platter.
items.ex: Según fuentes oficiales, el puente abre mañana.
items.exEn: According to official sources, the bridge opens tomorrow.

items.use: Masculine: el informe. 'Entregar un informe' = hand in a report.
items.ex: Tengo que entregar el informe el viernes.
items.exEn: I have to hand in the report on Friday.

items.use: 'A la izquierda' = on/to the left. 'La izquierda' is also the political left.
items.ex: Gira a la izquierda en el semáforo.
items.exEn: Turn left at the traffic light.

items.use: Human leg. For animals and furniture, use 'pata'.
items.ex: Me lastimé la pierna jugando fútbol.
items.exEn: I hurt my leg playing soccer.

items.use: 'La sala' = the living room. 'Sala de espera' = waiting room. 'Sala de cine' = movie theater.
items.ex: Los niños están viendo tele en la sala.
items.exEn: The kids are watching TV in the living room.

items.use: Phone signal, a road sign, or a gesture. 'No hay señal' = no signal.
items.ex: Aquí no hay señal de celular.
items.exEn: There's no cell signal here.

items.use: A sample (blood, product), a sign of something ('muestra de cariño') or an exhibition.
items.ex: Le sacaron una muestra de sangre.
items.exEn: They took a blood sample from him.

items.use: Your school grade ('sacar buena nota') or a written note. Also a musical note.
items.ex: Sacó una nota muy buena en el examen.
items.exEn: She got a very good grade on the test.

items.use: 'A la derecha' = on/to the right. Don't confuse with 'derecho' (straight ahead; also law/right). Also the political right.
items.ex: La farmacia está a la derecha.
items.exEn: The pharmacy is on the right.

items.use: A scene in a movie or play. 'Hacer una escena' = make a scene.
items.ex: Esa escena de la película me hizo llorar.
items.exEn: That scene in the movie made me cry.

items.use: Unit of length and the subway/metro. 'Metro cuadrado' = square meter.
items.ex: Tomo el metro para ir al trabajo.
items.exEn: I take the metro to work.
items.latam: Panama City has the first metro in Central America.

items.use: Entrance of a building, a ticket for an event, or the first course of a meal.
items.ex: Compré las entradas para el concierto.
items.exEn: I bought the tickets for the concert.
items.latam: For events, Panamanians also say 'boleto'.

items.use: 'Hacer un regalo' = give a gift. 'De regalo' = as a gift / free.
items.ex: Le compré un regalo a mi mamá.
items.exEn: I bought my mom a present.

items.use: Any large building, especially apartment towers.
items.ex: Vivo en un edificio de veinte pisos.
items.exEn: I live in a twenty-story building.

items.use: 'Sufrir de una enfermedad'. For a mild sickness, people say 'estar enfermo'.
items.ex: El dengue es una enfermedad común en la temporada lluviosa.
items.exEn: Dengue is a common illness in the rainy season.

items.use: A man's suit. 'Traje de baño' = swimsuit. 'Traje típico' = traditional dress.
items.ex: Tiene que ir de traje a la entrevista.
items.exEn: He has to wear a suit to the interview.
items.latam: Panama's 'pollera' is the national traditional dress ('traje típico').

items.use: 'Pedir disculpas' = apologize. 'Disculpa' / 'Disculpe' alone = excuse me.
items.ex: Te pido disculpas por llegar tarde.
items.exEn: I apologize for being late.

items.use: The evening meal. 'Cenar' is the verb.
items.ex: La cena está lista a las siete.
items.exEn: Dinner is ready at seven.

items.use: El/la guardia = a guard (person). 'La guardia' also = the duty itself: 'estar de guardia' = be on duty/on call.
items.ex: El guardia de seguridad abrió la puerta.
items.exEn: The security guard opened the door.
items.latam: In Panama a security guard is often called 'el seguridad'.

items.use: Economic or personal development. 'Países en desarrollo' = developing countries.
items.ex: El desarrollo de la ciudad ha sido muy rápido.
items.exEn: The city's development has been very fast.

items.use: Means 'matter/issue', not 'a question you ask' (that is 'pregunta'). 'Es cuestión de tiempo' = it's a matter of time.
items.ex: Es solo cuestión de tiempo.
items.exEn: It's just a matter of time.

items.use: 'Datos' = data, information. 'Datos personales' = personal details. On phones, 'datos' = mobile data.
items.ex: Se me acabaron los datos del celular.
items.exEn: I ran out of mobile data.

items.use: Similar to 'razón'. '¿Por qué motivo?' = for what reason?
items.ex: ¿Cuál es el motivo de su viaje?
items.exEn: What is the reason for your trip?

items.use: Usually a serious crime, often murder. For crime in general, 'la delincuencia'. Plural with accent: crímenes.
items.ex: La policía investiga el crimen.
items.exEn: The police are investigating the crime.

items.use: Feminine: la flor. 'Un ramo de flores' = a bouquet.
items.ex: Le regalé flores por su cumpleaños.
items.exEn: I gave her flowers for her birthday.

items.use: The ceremony and party. 'Ir a una boda'.
items.ex: La boda es en una iglesia del Casco Viejo.
items.exEn: The wedding is at a church in the Casco Viejo.

items.use: A single item or a unit in a book or the army. Also unity.
items.ex: Cada unidad cuesta dos dólares.
items.exEn: Each unit costs two dollars.

items.use: 'Un montón de' = a lot of (informal). 'Montones' = loads.
items.ex: Tengo un montón de trabajo esta semana.
items.exEn: I have a ton of work this week.

items.use: False friend: 'éxito' = success, not exit (exit = 'salida'). 'Tener éxito' = be successful.
items.ex: ¡Mucho éxito en tu nuevo trabajo!
items.exEn: Good luck in your new job!

items.use: 'Estar en peligro' = be in danger. '¡Peligro!' on signs.
items.ex: Esa calle es un peligro de noche.
items.exEn: That street is dangerous at night.

items.use: 'Darse un golpe' = bump yourself. 'De golpe' = suddenly. 'Golpe de Estado' = coup.
items.ex: Me di un golpe en la rodilla.
items.exEn: I banged my knee.

items.use: 'Productos de limpieza' = cleaning products. Also produce from a farm.
items.ex: Este producto está en oferta.
items.exEn: This product is on sale.

items.use: Feminine: la carne. Often means beef specifically. 'Carne de res' = beef.
items.ex: ¿Prefieres carne o pescado?
items.exEn: Do you prefer meat or fish?
items.latam: 'Carne en palito' (meat on a stick) is a classic Panamanian street food.

items.use: 'Es un placer' = it's a pleasure. 'Con placer' = gladly.
items.ex: Es un placer conocerlo.
items.exEn: It's a pleasure to meet you.

items.use: House windows and computer windows. A car or bank window is 'ventanilla'.
items.ex: ¿Puedes abrir la ventana? Hace calor.
items.exEn: Can you open the window? It's hot.

items.use: 'De oro' = made of gold. 'Medalla de oro' = gold medal.
items.ex: Le regaló un anillo de oro.
items.exEn: He gave her a gold ring.

items.use: An action ('en el acto' = on the spot) or a formal event ('acto de graduación').
items.ex: El acto de graduación empieza a las diez.
items.exEn: The graduation ceremony starts at ten.

items.use: Feminine: la cárcel. 'Ir a la cárcel', 'estar en la cárcel'.
items.ex: Lo mandaron a la cárcel por cinco años.
items.exEn: They sent him to prison for five years.

items.use: For the device, Panama and most of LatAm say 'el radio'; for broadcasting, 'la radio'. 'El radio' is also a radius.
items.ex: Escuché la noticia en la radio.
items.exEn: I heard the news on the radio.
items.latam: Spain says 'la radio' for both the device and broadcasting.

items.use: Also an adjective: 'el país enemigo'.
items.ex: No quiero ser tu enemigo.
items.exEn: I don't want to be your enemy.

items.use: Feminine but takes 'el': el hambre. Use 'tener hambre' (not 'estar'), and 'mucha hambre'.
items.ex: Tengo mucha hambre, ¿comemos?
items.exEn: I'm really hungry, shall we eat?

items.use: A department in a company or store. In some countries also an apartment.
items.ex: Trabajo en el departamento de ventas.
items.exEn: I work in the sales department.
items.latam: In Panama an apartment is 'apartamento'; 'departamento' for a flat is used in Mexico, Peru, Argentina and Chile.

items.use: The floor you walk on and a level of a building: 'vivo en el piso 10'.
items.ex: Vivo en el quinto piso.
items.exEn: I live on the fifth floor.
items.latam: In Spain 'piso' also means an apartment; in Panama it does not.

items.use: 'Me duele la espalda' = my back hurts. 'De espaldas' = with your back turned.
items.ex: Me duele la espalda de tanto manejar.
items.exEn: My back hurts from so much driving.

items.use: A woman's dress. Masculine word: el vestido. 'Vestido de novia' = wedding dress.
items.ex: Se compró un vestido rojo para la fiesta.
items.exEn: She bought a red dress for the party.

items.use: 'Al norte de' = north of. Capitalized in names: 'América del Norte'.
items.ex: Chiriquí está al oeste, no al norte.
items.exEn: Chiriquí is to the west, not the north.

items.use: An aspect of something, or someone's look: 'tener buen aspecto' = look well.
items.ex: Tienes muy buen aspecto hoy.
items.exEn: You look really well today.

items.use: A visit and also guests: 'tenemos visita' = we have company. Always feminine, even for a man.
items.ex: Hoy tenemos visita, así que limpia tu cuarto.
items.exEn: We have guests today, so clean your room.

items.use: 'Hacer una broma' = play a joke. 'En broma' = jokingly. A told joke is often 'chiste'.
items.ex: No te enojes, era una broma.
items.exEn: Don't get mad, it was a joke.

items.use: '¡Qué sorpresa!' = what a surprise! 'Fiesta sorpresa' = surprise party.
items.ex: Le hicimos una fiesta sorpresa.
items.exEn: We threw him a surprise party.

items.use: A court trial, or good sense: 'perder el juicio' = lose your mind.
items.ex: El juicio empieza la próxima semana.
items.exEn: The trial starts next week.

items.use: Feminine: la defensa. Also the defense in sports and in court.
items.ex: Actuó en defensa propia.
items.exEn: He acted in self-defense.

items.use: A rule ('las reglas del juego') or a ruler for measuring. Also means a woman's period.
items.ex: Esas son las reglas de la casa.
items.exEn: Those are the house rules.

items.use: A group of people or a neighborhood. 'Comunidad indígena'.
items.ex: La comunidad organizó una limpieza de la playa.
items.exEn: The community organized a beach cleanup.
